entries.headline: Back to one source of truth — and the rules so it stays that way
entries.summary: Four parallel worktrees converged to main in a single day (#60–#64): the document knowledge base shipped Phase A plus A.5 retrieval hardening and the first two Phase-B stories (YED-118/156/157), the Inbox Intelligence Miner landed as a first-class market-intelligence signal source with its own ADR (YED-153), the OBS capture lane replaced the dead Granola path (YED-154), and the job-search content rulings plus a roadmap reconcile cleared a five-item decision backlog. Convergence worked on its own; what didn't was everything around it.  — Second ship: the build-quality judge caught ADR-8 Increment 1 claiming a scope it had not held — a quorum split, Gemini 1.0 against Sonnet 0.55 — and the flagging seat was right. The system graph was persisting edge types nothing read, a direct violation of the ADR's own rule, and one git subprocess per artifact had put the rebuild at ~5s against a stated <2s. Fixed by deletion (0.2s, roughly 25× faster), the false "scope held" claim struck in place rather than quietly rewritten, and a --selftest added so the extractor cannot regress silently (#65). A decision record that shows its own wrong claim is worth more than one that hides it.  — Third ship: the reconciliation itself. The chaos was never branches — code had self-merged unprompted — it was sessions: three Claude sessions shared the main checkout while it sat on a feature branch, each believing another one owned it, and Linear carried six shipped issues still marked Backlog. Converged from a scratch worktree with server-side PRs (the charter's quiesce-first rule could not be met, so the method routed around it), corrected Linear to git truth, retired a four-month-stale priorities block, wrote the git conventions into CLAUDE.md and the reconciliation charter into the repo, rescued five machine-local plan files that two ADRs still cited, and sharded the telemetry ledger per session so the one file every worktree appended to can never conflict again (#67, #68; YED-159). Still open: the denylist review that gates the whole-inbox scan, and ADR-7's acceptance sits in review (#69). The value: a repo where "what's open" and "what shipped" finally agree, and the failure mode written down before it recurs.  — Fourth entry, the pipeline in use rather than under construction: /check-new-events ran against the coming week and found nine events on the calendar, none carrying a PIPELINE block, so the raw-calendar fallback did the intake — Luma, Meetup and the Gmail registration receipts resolved what the invites truncated (the Notion-hosted "Context is King" webinar, Miracle Software's middleware pitch, the seven names on the LeadDev agenda, Ryan Booz of pganalyze). Dedup against Notion came back empty, the Deep Read ledger was clean, the renderer was registered: a clean start, and one calendar defect caught before it cost a missed session (the Goldcast receipt says 1pm ET; the invite said 9am).  — Fifth entry, the run stopping exactly where it is designed to: nine full briefs do not fit one session — each research fan-out spends roughly 40–70 of a ~200-search cap — so the pipeline surfaced a tiering call (four in-person rooms plus the RevGenius system-of-action panel now, two vendor livestreams next session, two webinars roundup-only) and held at the Step 5 gate with the steering intake batched into the same reply. Nothing was written to Notion. Still open: the go on the tier split. The value: the human-in-the-loop design holding under a real week's load, and a hard constraint doing the prioritization the calendar never does.  — Sixth entry, what the flagged build actually is: ADR-8 Increment 1 is a derived graph over the repo's own build artifacts — every skill, command, hook, ADR and the references between them — rebuilt by a stdlib-only extractor on SessionStart and Stop hooks. The point was never the graph; it was that the rigor layer had been good at recording and bad at watching, because every control was invoked (a command someone types) rather than triggered. Proof it flipped: an ordinary `git mv` on a referenced file surfaced a finding at the next session start naming all three citing sites, with nobody invoking anything. It also turned up two defects in `check-refs.sh` — the tool it generalizes, and the one feeding the judge's completeness cap: first that path templates like `evolution-log-{slug}.md` were being reported as missing files, so the cap had been firing on artifacts whose references were never broken; then that the fix over-corrected and began swallowing real broken references sharing a line with a template, which is a reference checker hiding references. Both are pinned now by the extractor's self-test, whose second assertion checks the two tools still agree — the ADR says their rules are shared verbatim, and until now that was enforced by a comment reading "change both", which cannot enforce itself. The value: the check that guards every other build finally has a check of its own (#61, #65).

entries.headline: The job search becomes a system
entries.summary: Shipped Job-Search Engine v1 (Phase A+B, YED-146–152): repositioned role-radar from a generic scanner into a Target-Role ICP filter anchored on the me-model — the candidate source-of-truth authored days earlier — then ran it live end-to-end, 158 roles scored into the Notion Roles DB. Hardened the rubric from that real run: exemptions so good roles don't drop on a technicality (hybrid new+existing, PLG-primary, an intangibles lever), an IC-vs-people-management gate (does the role carry a personal book?), and a wider title keep-list that closes real misses (Sierra, Snorkel) — every exemption reasoned in Notes so it's auditable. Cross-provider quorum judged PASS (Sonnet 0.81 / Gemini 1.0), with 7 leadership roles JD-verified and demoted A→C in the same run. The value: the parallel job search stops being ad-hoc browsing and becomes an instrumented, ICP-scored pipeline that sharpens itself from its own output (#56).

entries.headline: Reps on the host's own stack, as the demo
entries.summary: Scaffolded Signal Stream — a real-time GTM signal agent built on Confluent's own stack (Kafka + Flink ML_PREDICT + managed MCP + RAG) — as warm-up for Confluent AI Day NYC, so the prep doubles as reps on the event's stack and a working opener for the Confluent-for-Startups lead. Built in three independently-demoable layers: query a live topic in natural language → classify each stream event against the ICP into Notion → a stretch multi-agent situation room; stdlib-only, with the producer and sink tested against live data. Deliberately scaffold-only, with the fast-moving Flink AI SQL flagged in-file as needs-verifying rather than claimed working — honest about what compiles versus what's proven. The value: it turns event attendance into a demo on the room's own terms — the documentarian edge applied to a hackathon (#55). The Confluent AI Day carousel shipped alongside.

entries.headline: Co-creation gets a real gate, and the content finally gets a mirror
entries.summary: Split the pre-research steering interview into two touches (YED-143): a light, skippable Aim before the research fan-out, and a Sharpen gate after the brief that puts ≤3 genuine forks — derived from what the prep actually surfaced — to Alex before drafting. The insight: real co-creation comes from informed forks that only exist after the research ("the transcript leaned on X but your angle says Y — which post?"), not generic up-front prompts, so the fix was to split the intake, not move it; wired to auto-fire across five content flows.  — Second ship (hub): the Content Performance dashboard, a point-in-time read of 50 LinkedIn posts answering the question under the whole post-performance thread — who does the content actually reach? It surfaced the topic→audience finding (GTM posts reach founders+GTM 54%, technical posts reach engineers 65%), visuals out-engaging text ~2.4×, and a reach≠resonance gap — and cleared the repo's pre-existing lint so the hub build goes green again. The value: the pipeline now co-creates by construction, and Alex can finally see whether the audience he's reaching is the one he's targeting (#54, hub #13).

entries.headline: The gate that can't close green on a thin brief
entries.summary: Turned the Deep Read from a step you could silently skip into one the run fails without. A local ledger marks each event pending at commit and rendered only on success; a fail-closed Stop hook plus an in-conversation marker re-check then fail any run that closes with an unrendered Deep Read — and, most importantly, write it to a durable failure log so a thin brief can't stay invisible the way 38 of them did on Aug 24. The prior fix (YED-138) was prose discipline an agent can skip; this is mechanical. Adversarially reviewed (four real false-green/invisibility holes found and fixed), quorum-judged PASS, DoD closed, with the residual-hardening edges logged as a follow-up rather than overclaimed.  — Second ship: a pronoun-fidelity rule in the brief renderer — never infer a person's pronouns from their name, default they/them until a source confirms — after it silently misgendered a real speaker from their name. Small rule, but it stops a real person being mislabeled in content Alex may tag them in; the parallel name-fidelity fix also got its long-pending validation cleared in the same render.

entries.headline: A better brief and a truer voice
entries.summary: Wired the research brief v2: one artifact with a phone-glanceable Scan head in the room, and a deep, cited, novice-friendly prose “commute read” rendered afterward and appended without ever blocking the pipeline. The old output had regressed to a machine-readable bullet lattice; this restores flowing analysis and adds a historical spine, inline-defined jargon, and end-to-end source citations. The value is a briefing worth reading on the train that walks Alex into a room genuinely conversant — and a richer substrate every downstream post draws from.  — Second ship of the day: the audience-first ethos went from charter to production (YED-103). The north-star document existed but no content skill actually read it, so posts kept drifting back to self-as-protagonist; this wired it into the six content surfaces and codified the “ordering, not erasure” counterweight (so “decenter yourself” stops collapsing into self-erasure that reads junior to a buyer), the three floors, a softened voice rule, and a mandatory 3–5 “learn more” citation set on every post. The value: the pipeline now generates audience-first content by construction, not just on paper — shipped, judged pass cross-provider, DoD closed.  — Third ship: the brief-v2 wiring finally got its live end-to-end acceptance test, which last session's frozen agent registry made impossible. Ran the whole pipeline on a real event (Elastic NYC × Plural) — four specialists, synthesizer, five Notion writes, then the Deep Read rendered section-by-section on Opus and appended decoupled. The render cleared the Daytona spike bar and closed its one open gap: endnotes now carry real source URLs end to end (specialist ledger → synthesizer evidence set → renderer), quorum-judged PASS (Sonnet 0.896 / Gemini 1.0). It also caught a genuine renderer bug — confabulated speaker first names in the sections where the speakers were only passing references — corrected in-run and then hardened out of the spec so the standing pipeline reproduces names verbatim. Decoupling held: the Scan head and every entity record committed independently of the render. The value: brief-v2 is proven in production rather than merely wired, with the one real defect found and fixed before merge (#47).

entries.headline: The cross-provider judge
entries.summary: Wired a second, cross-provider judge (Gemini alongside Sonnet) into the build-quality gate and mechanized the dangling-reference check. An LLM grading its own model family self-prefers; a different provider is the cheapest robust mitigation. Build quality now gets an independent, adversarial second opinion instead of a rubber stamp.

entries.headline: Closing the rigor loop + judge calibration
entries.summary: Calibrated the judge against a human anchor — crossing the trust gate to provisional-trusted — and wired the missing writer so DoD telemetry fields stop coming back null. Rigor that isn't written to the execution path decays silently. Rigor became measurable where the work actually happens, not in an optional doc.

entries.headline: The command-orchestration convention
entries.summary: Authored the required command skeleton (intake → dispatch → collect → synthesize → named output) after a thin, declarative command failed the quality bar, and ran live LLM-as-judge execution. A command that only lists agents without dispatch/output logic isn't done. Commands now meet a completeness standard the judge can enforce.
